briefing.text: This dataset appears to be a gastric adenocarcinoma whole-exome study (center pfizer_uhongkong, GRCh37, with Lauren and EBV/H. pylori fields). Confirm CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED and that a Lauren histology field (PATHOLOGY_LAUREN) exists; if so, a hypothesis about RHOA in diffuse-type gastric tumours concerns this study's own cohort and genes, and under the task's labelling convention should be decided as True or False rather than Not verifiable.
briefing.reason: Choosing the label category (on-topic vs Not verifiable) is the first decision and a wrong Not verifiable is graded wrong.

briefing.text: The hypothesis has two parts: RHOA mutation frequency of about 14.3% in diffuse-type tumours, and no RHOA mutations in intestinal-type tumours. Report exact counts k/n per Lauren group (diffuse, intestinal, and mixed/other separately) with exact binomial confidence intervals, and check whether 14.3% corresponds to a simple fraction of the diffuse count (e.g. 1/7). Evaluate both parts; note that figures from the publication may come from a discovery cohort that differs from the deposited subset.
briefing.reason: Both components can independently decide the label; teams must test each explicitly.

briefing.text: Lauren histology is in data_clinical_patient.txt (PATHOLOGY_LAUREN) while mutations are keyed by Tumor_Sample_Barcode; join via the sample table (PATIENT_ID to SAMPLE_ID) and confirm each sample maps to one patient. Denominators must be all sequenced samples of each Lauren type from the clinical tables, not only samples that appear in data_mutations.txt (wild-type samples have no RHOA row). List PATHOLOGY_LAUREN value counts including mixed/unknown/NA.
briefing.reason: Wrong joins or denominators change the frequency being compared to 14.3%.

briefing.text: Tabulate RHOA Variant_Classification and HGVSp. Count unique samples with non-synonymous RHOA variants (missense, nonsense, frameshift, splice, in-frame), excluding silent/intronic/UTR calls and not double-counting tumours with multiple RHOA mutations. Known RHOA hotspots in diffuse gastric cancer include R5, G17, Y42 and L57; report hotspot and non-hotspot hits separately.
briefing.reason: Variant filtering and per-sample counting directly determine the numerator.

briefing.text: If any intestinal-type tumour carries a RHOA mutation, cross-tabulate it with MSI status and mutation burden (TMB) and check whether it is a known hotspot, since hypermutated MSI-high tumours (mostly intestinal) carry many passenger mutations. Report this explicitly when judging the 'not in intestinal-type' part.
briefing.reason: Interpretation of any intestinal RHOA hit hinges on whether it is a driver or a passenger in a hypermutated tumour.
